claim: The tweezers' interlocks are built into low-level electronics hardware, independent of the computer and its software, and wherever possible a safety measure is mechanical, such as the shutter, so that it does not depend on electrical power.
validity_conditions: Read from Tweez 305/310 Laser Safety Manual V3.0, November 2022, as installed in C:/Program Files/Aresis/Tweez300/Manuals/ (sha256 264ab54b...): printed page 4 (PDF page 6), printed page 9 (PDF page 11). E3 vendor_spec: the manufacturer's statement, not an observation on this bench. So a software failure is not supposed to defeat an interlock; a hardware fault is a different question this manual does not address. KNOWLEDGE, NOT POLICY: this is what the manufacturer says. What any session may do, and every limit anyone here acts on, is the person's, written into the envelope after confirming it on the instrument.
